newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila overnight money holds but rates seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Manila overnight money holds but rates seen rising.

text.p: * Volume falls to 18.57 bln from 21.28 bln pesos
Manila overnight money remained at an average of 10.28125 percent on Tuesday but the market expected interest rates to rise in the short term, traders said.
"Right now, interest rates will depend a lot on the stock market," a foreign bank dealer said.
The equities market took another beating on Tuesday due to heavy foreign selling. Traders said this would put pressure on the peso and force the Central Bank to increase rates.
Rates moved in a wider range from 10.75 to 10.28125 percent, with 34 lenders and 20 borrowers.
"There's a wait-and-see attitude right now," another dealer said.
It led banks to just hold the T-bills they bought at the auction yesterday, traders said.
The secondary market saw thin trade with banks buying short-term bills to meet clients' requirements, dealers said.
A Reuters poll of seven banks gave bid rates of 10.35 to 10.50 percent for the three-month bills.
